verdict.reasoning: Patient says, “I've been having this blinding headache for a few days…,” and later clarifies it started three days ago: “I woke up one morning with a headache, and that was three days ago.”

Headache onset and duration: “It just started all of a sudden. I woke up one morning with a headache, and that was three days ago… I just keep having [it].” Partial relief with ibuprofen: “It doesn't really go away without ibuprofen either… It gets a little bit better, but doesn't go away.”
Severity: “I guess it's mostly eight, and then it comes down to maybe a five.”
Location: “It's kind of all over, but I feel like over my right eye is a bit stronger,” indicating bilateral/general with right-sided predominance.
Photophobia: “Lights definitely make me more sensitive. I don't really like strong lights.”
Visual disturbance: “Yeah, vision. I think I get this shooting light sometimes… Just a bit of a weird kind of vision.”
Nausea: When asked about nausea/vomiting, patient replies, “No, I'm feeling a bit sick, but no vomiting,” which is consistent with mild nausea.

No prior similar severe headaches: “Not really. Just the on and off… So nothing like for longer than two days before,” and clinician notes, “it's obviously the first time you've had such a bad headache.”

Impact on work: “I work from home, but couldn't really manage to do it all the time… today I just tried to work from home the first half of the day, but I just stopped in the morning because I couldn't focus.”
Past abdominal pain: “I think I only had the abdominal pain when I was younger, but no cause was found and that went away.”
Ibuprofen use: “I… had one… but it just went away with ibuprofen,” and later, “apart from the ibuprofen I take sometimes and the headache gets really bad.”
OCP: “Just the pill.” / “Which one?” / “Marcelone.”
Allergies: When asked, “And any allergies to anything?” patient replies, “No.”
Family history: “my mum suffers from, like, she has migraines… She's like. Has the vomiting and everything.”
Living situation: In response to “Who do you live with at home?” patient states, “Just by myself.”
Smoking status: “And do you smoke?” / “No.”
Alcohol: “How much in a normal week…?” / “Probably like three beers once a Week.”
Drugs: “Do you take any other drugs at all?” / “No, apart from the ibuprofen I take sometimes…” indicating no illicit/recreational drug use.
Work: “Been at work recently?” / “I work from home…”
Eye exam: “have you had any eye checks recently?” / “Yeah, actually had one recently and nothing changed my vision.”

Blood pressure: “Your blood pressure checked recently with your pill?” / “Yeah, I had it checked in the pharmacy when I got the pill and they said it was normal.” / “And when was that?” / “A year ago.”

Persistent headache with migraine-like features: 3 days constant (“I just keep having [it].”), photophobia (“Lights definitely make me more sensitive”), visual disturbance (“shooting light”), and impact on daily activities/work (“couldn't really manage… because I couldn't focus”). These are migraine-like features even though the exact wording is from the summarizing fact.
Migraine considered: Clinician says, “it could possibly be a migraine type headache,” and later, “Because if we do think it's a migraine…”
Medication plan: “I can prescribe you something similar to ibuprofen, but a bit stronger… and you can take paracetamol at the same time.” This is a stronger NSAID plus paracetamol.
Neurological exam: “we probably should book you into an appointment to get an examination… we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well.”

Components of exam: “we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well,” and later, “we'll check your blood pressure as well, just to make sure your pill is still appropriate for you.” This corresponds to neuro exam, fundoscopy, and BP check.

AE referral if worse: “if in the meantime, before your appointment, your headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing, then if it's that bad, then you should go to AE and have an examination.”

Review pill if migraine: “Because if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights and things like that… that pill… wouldn't be suitable to stay on that pill particularly. We'd have to change it something else.”
